last_analysis: No scores are visible, so I can only choose from priors and from which trials trained cleanly. All 9 trials trained without errors. The layer-aware landing head is the idea that best matches the task: whether a placement is right depends on which layer the brick lands in and whether that layer is missing cells there. Its latest version, r3c1, adds z-cumulative features and a landing gate. It uses about 1.5x the starting compute and trains for 278k steps, well inside the time and compute limits. Recipes that see more fresh designs (1 epoch, 512 envs) give 2–3x more samples. That should help generalisation to unseen designs. In this final round I refine r3c1 in three ways, one main change each: (1) the legal-action mask as a learned input to the head, (2) cheap per-layer spatial context from a depthwise 3x3 conv, and (3) a recipe change to 32-step rollouts with lower entropy.
